chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sahkuni al-Muzakki in Kufa in the year 354 A.H. narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hadrami narrated to us: Al-Qasim ibn Zakariya ibn Dinar narrated to us: Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us: Ja'far al-Ahmar, from Ummi al-Sayrafi, from Abu Kathir al-Ansari, from Abdullah ibn As'ad ibn Zurarah

He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: My Lord ascended me [to the heavens] and revealed to me regarding Ali (peace be upon him) three [things]: Indeed, he is the leader of the pious, the master of the believers, and the commander of those with radiant foreheads.

key_terms.قَائِدُ الْغُرِّ الْمُحَجَّلِينَ: Commander of those with radiant foreheads

ai.seo_question: What three titles did God reveal for Imam Ali during the Prophet's ascension?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal* links the Imamate of Ali ibn Abi Talib directly to the Prophet’s Mi'raj, emphasizing its divine origin rather than mere human designation. The triad of titles—Imam of the Pious, Master of Believers, and Leader of the Radiant Ones—underscores Ali’s unique spiritual authority and his role as the exemplar for the faithful, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegetical tradition regarding the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-94 In Kufa in the year 354 A.H. (965 A.D.) Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad al-Sahkooni al-Mazaki narrated that Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hazrami quoted on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Zakaria ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ishaq ibn Mansoor, on the authority of Ja’far al-Ahmar, on theauthority of Ummi al-Sayrafi, on the authority of Abi Kathir al-Ansari, on the authority of Abdullah ibn As’ad ibn Zurarah

that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “When I ascended to my Lord, He revealed to me three words regarding Ali (MGB): he is the leader of the pious ones; he is the master of the believers; and he is the leader of the radiant ones.”
